headline: Freedmen’s Hospital housed medical trainees
description: Around 1933, Freedmen’s Hospital built a residence for its interns and residents. It offered specialty training to Black physicians during segregation, when many hospitals excluded them. Howard University Hospital later replaced Freedmen’s as Howard’s teaching hospital.
sourceTitle: Howard University College of Medicine · History

headline: Freedmen’s opens classrooms and housing for nursing students
description: Freedmen’s Hospital, the predecessor of Howard University Hospital, ran its own school of nursing. In 1941 it opened a building on Howard’s campus where nursing students lived and attended classes.
sourceTitle: Howard University College of Medicine · History of Freedmen’s Hospital

headline: Howard West brought computer science students to Google
description: The 2017 pilot provided a three-month computer-science education program at Google. In September 2018, Google reported that 26 students completed the pilot and half had obtained engineering internships at Google or elsewhere in the industry.
sourceTitle: Howard University College of Engineering and Architecture · Howard West
sourceNote: This is Google's report of one cohort. Internships are not permanent jobs, and participation is not evidence of a connection to an individual reader.

moreSources.title: Google · Tech Exchange brings Black and Latinx students to Google

headline: Engineering internships for students at partner HBCUs
description: Boeing’s 2026 scholar program offered engineering internships to students at partner HBCUs, including Tuskegee University and North Carolina A&T State University. The program paired consecutive internships with scholarships and mentoring.
sourceTitle: Thurgood Marshall College Fund · Boeing Corporate Programs
fromInstitution: Partner HBCUs, including Tuskegee and North Carolina A&T

aliases: Meharry Medical College School of Dentistry
headline: Dental education at Meharry
description: Meharry’s School of Dentistry identifies Black dental practitioners among those it seeks to mentor and train. Its current mission and program page lists general practice and pediatric dentistry residencies but does not date the start of those opportunities.
sourceTitle: Meharry School of Dentistry · Mission, vision and programs

aliases: CHI St. Vincent Hot Springs Hospital
headline: Morehouse and CommonSpirit announced a medical training partnership
description: The medical school and health system announced a partnership to expand training for underrepresented clinicians in December 2020. A later CommonSpirit account identifies Morehouse as academic sponsor of the internal medicine residency at CHI St. Vincent Hot Springs. The announcement date is for the partnership.
sourceTitle: CommonSpirit Health · St. Vincent Hot Springs training site

headline: Howard’s journalism partnership with NBCU Academy
description: In 2022, Howard University’s communications school joined NBCU Academy, the NBCUniversal News Group’s journalism training program. The partnership connected Howard students with newsroom instruction and journalists across the network.
sourceTitle: Howard University · Howard joins NBCU Academy

headline: Howard University Hospital replaces Freedmen’s Hospital

paperMilestone.headline: Anna B. Coles leads Howard’s new nursing school
paperMilestone.description: Under founding dean Anna B. Coles, a Freedmen’s nursing graduate, Howard introduced its bachelor’s program in 1969. Its first class graduated in 1973.
paperMilestone.previewDetail: Its first bachelor’s class graduated in 1973.
paperMilestone.sourceTitle: Freedmen’s nursing alumni · The founding dean

sourceNote: Howard’s hospital history dates the opening of the successor hospital. Its medical school history separately describes training facilities for nurses at Freedmen’s.
description: Howard University Hospital opened as the successor to Freedmen’s Hospital. This is the documented institutional link between the earlier teaching hospital and the workplace you entered.
sourceTitle: Howard University College of Medicine · Howard University Hospital

headline: Atlanta’s school board replaces separate pay schedules
description: After William H. Reeves challenged teacher pay in 1942, Atlanta’s school board abolished its separate salary schedules and called for one plan. A later lawsuit challenged whether Black teachers actually received equal pay.
sourceTitle: Fifth Circuit · Cook v. Davis

headline: Melvin O. Alston challenges Norfolk’s racial pay gap
description: Alston taught at Norfolk’s Booker T. Washington High School and joined the Norfolk Teachers’ Association in challenging lower pay for Black teachers. The Fourth Circuit reversed the dismissal and sent the case back for further proceedings.
sourceTitle: Fourth Circuit · Alston v. School Board of City of Norfolk

headline: IN-Tech trains electrical apprentices
sourceNote: The institute describes its registration and selection process. The guide leaves individual admission and hiring decisions unknown.

headline: Sam Taylor starts an electrical contracting company
paperTitle: Sam Taylor and Charles Stewart start Taylor Electric

paperMilestone.headline: Taylor Electric maintains Soldier Field
paperMilestone.description: Taylor Electric lists Soldier Field in its project portfolio. The union’s account dates the start of electrical maintenance there to the early 1990s.
paperMilestone.sourceNote: The contractor lists the stadium project. The union supplies the period when electrical maintenance began. Neither record identifies an individual crew member.

sourceNote: The HistoryMakers’ biography describes a friend ordering lessons that publishers would not send to Black readers. Stewart and Taylor studied the trade before starting the company.
description: Sam Taylor and Charles Vernon Stewart III studied the trade together when publishers refused to send electrical lessons to Black readers. Stewart helped Taylor start the company in Chicago in 1922.

aliases: International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 134, Chicago, IL
headline: Black electricians gain full membership in Local 134
sourceNote: Stewart’s interview guide distinguishes work permits from full union membership. It dates the change to 1943.
description: Charles Stewart recalled that Black electricians in Chicago first received work permits and later gained full union membership. He went on to help other Black electricians enter Local 134.
sourceTitle: The HistoryMakers · Charles Stewart’s interview guide

headline: Taylor Electric takes on stadium maintenance
sourceNote: The union identifies the contractor responsible for electrical maintenance. Its account leaves the names of individual crew members unknown.

sourceTitle: IBEW · Taylor Electric’s Chicago projects

headline: Three nurses win a ruling against discriminatory dismissal
description: They challenged their dismissal; the appeals court rejected the hospital’s defense and reversed the lower court. The court directed reinstatement offers and recognized entitlement to back pay, reduced by interim earnings. The opinion establishes ordered relief at this hospital, not evidence that every remedy was carried out or that all nursing workplaces changed.
sourceNote: The opinion establishes ordered relief at this hospital, not evidence that every remedy was carried out or that all nursing workplaces changed. This names the historical hospital; a connection to a renamed or successor employer needs a separate record.
sourceTitle: Smith v. Hampton Training School for Nurses · 360 F.2d 577

headline: Samuel Battle enters the NYPD and later reaches supervisory ranks
description: He was sworn in as a police officer in 1911. He became a sergeant in 1926 and a lieutenant in 1935, documenting advancement as well as entry. His career establishes particular appointments; it does not explain the selection process or promotion chances for every Black officer.
sourceNote: His career establishes particular appointments; it does not explain the selection process or promotion chances for every Black officer.
sourceTitle: NYC Department of Records · City Hall Library Notes, April 2016

headline: Xerox’s board elects Ursula Burns chief executive
description: On May 21, the board elected Burns CEO with an effective date of July 1, 2009. The company filed the decision publicly; Mulcahy was to remain board chair, distinguishing the two positions. The filing establishes an appointment decision at Xerox, not a change in hiring rules for every Black employee or an appointment at another employer.
sourceNote: The filing establishes an appointment decision at Xerox, not a change in hiring rules for every Black employee or an appointment at another employer.
sourceTitle: Xerox Corporation · May 21, 2009 Form 8-K

headline: George Washington Carver becomes Tuskegee’s director of agriculture
description: After agricultural degrees at Iowa State in 1894 and 1896, Carver joined Tuskegee’s staff. The National Park Service dates his appointment as director of agriculture to October 8, 1896.
sourceTitle: National Park Service · George Washington Carver at Tuskegee
sourceNote: This establishes Carver’s education and appointment at Tuskegee. It does not establish a hiring pathway for farmworkers or for another institution’s scientists.

headline: Thomas Campbell takes Tuskegee’s agricultural teaching to farmers
description: The Jesup Agricultural Wagon carried tools, seeds and demonstrations into farming communities. Campbell’s extension assignment connected a Black agricultural educator’s work to farmers in Macon County, Alabama.
sourceTitle: Smithsonian NMAAHC · Tuskegee Institute’s Movable Schools
sourceNote: This documents an educational service and a named assignment. It does not identify every participant or measure the program’s effect on each farm’s income.

headline: FAMU and Black food organizers open an agroecology center
description: They created the Lola Hampton-Frank Pinder Center for Agroecology at FAMU. Local reporting documented the November opening at the Orange Avenue garden, with classroom, laboratory and community-garden uses.
sourceTitle: National Black Food & Justice Alliance · FAMU agroecology center launch
sourceNote: The opening and named leadership are documented. The sources do not establish participant completion, paid placements or a particular reader’s employment.

moreSources.title: WFSU · Florida A&M University opens its new Agroecology Center

aliases: Office of the Governor of Virginia
headline: L. Douglas Wilder wins Virginia’s governorship
description: After serving in the state senate and as lieutenant governor, Wilder won the gubernatorial election in 1989. He began his term on January 14, 1990, and served through January 15, 1994.
sourceTitle: National Governors Association · L. Douglas Wilder
sourceNote: This records one statewide electoral breakthrough. It does not establish that a particular earlier governor caused the victory, or that every public-sector career became accessible.

aliases: Office of the Governor of Maryland
headline: Wes Moore is sworn in as Maryland’s first Black governor
description: Following the election, Moore took the oath of office on January 18, 2023. He entered service as Maryland’s 63rd governor, documented by the state biography and a same-day county statement from an attendee.
sourceTitle: Maryland Office of the Governor · Wes Moore
sourceNote: The officeholding record is established. Effects on a particular occupation, agency or worker require separate policies, appointment records and implementation evidence.

moreSources.title: Montgomery County · Statement on Moore and Miller’s inaugurations

sourceTitle: Georgia Public Broadcasting · Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Georgia’s governor race
